A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NUDGING by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-distribution analyses, benchmark evaluations, model-scaling experiments, and generated-answer case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds timing measurements, discarded-token analysis, Llama-3 evaluations, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 6 changes the intervention condition from top-1 probability > gamma to < gamma, correcting its inconsistency with the low-confidence intervention rule already described in v1. Word-based handoffs, stopping rules, and repetition controls remain unchanged; this supports a pseudocode correction, not an implemented-method redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 13-task coverage spanning reasoning, knowledge, open-ended instructions, and safety. The new task breakdown and constrained-instruction example use existing just-eval-instruct coverage. Llama-3 adds model configurations, not datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The 200-sample comparison in v1 Table 8 includes large-base, small-aligned, and large-aligned controls that are omitted from v3 Table 10. These controls remain in the main 1000-sample comparison. Average Ensemble and Proxy Tuning remain unchanged as the principal inference-time baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3 8B/70B evaluation settings, a 100-prompt Gemma-2 timing comparison, and case-insensitive LLC rescoring. It also changes the stated non-math and instruction evaluator from GPT-4 to GPT-4o. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not necessarily rerunning: v1's safety caption already names GPT-4o. The main zero-shot, greedy-decoding setup remains.

E4.justification: v3 adds task-specific instruction analysis (Figure 4), discarded-token diagnostics (Appendix C.2), a constrained-instruction failure case (Table 11), and LLC case-sensitivity analysis (Appendix E.2). Conversely, Figure 5 drops the Llama-2 scaling study, and alternative-threshold result tables are reduced, although the threshold-sweep curves remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Token-level model confidence and the new deterministic discarded-token bound do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 retain their scores, but v3 adds Llama-3, task-category, timing, and discarded-token results. Alignment-position recall at gamma=0.5 changes from over 90% in v1 Figure 3 to approximately 83% in v3 Figure 2. Table 6 replaces cross-family scores, including G+O GSM8K 41.0 to 43.3; its control values also shift from the 200-sample to 1000-sample table values, precluding a clean same-setting gain claim. Some threshold/control rows, Llama-2 scaling results, and the OLMo instruction radar are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an auxiliary derivation absent from v1: under its stated generation assumptions, the discarded-token ratio satisfies RD <= L/(1/RN + L - 1). The existing rank-based definition of alignment-related positions remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central training-free alignment, small-model guidance, and cross-family collaboration claims persist. v3 explicitly scopes alignment primarily to instruction following in the Introduction footnote and introduces an approximately 20-fold speed claim there, beyond v1's eightfold runtime statement in the experiments.

C2.justification: New limitations and Appendix E explain failures when the nudging model lacks necessary skills or post-training adds substantive capabilities, as illustrated by Llama-3. v3 also discusses discarded-token costs, English-only applicability, broader alignment issues left untested, and potentially harmful nudging models. These substantially qualify the earlier account of alignment as separable stylistic guidance.

D1.justification: v3 documents the timing workload and API/prefix-processing costs in Appendix C.1, while removing explicit gamma labels from the retained individual examples. Existing vLLM/A6000 information, completion and generation limits, prompts, repetition heuristics, and project access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Tulu 3, the GPT-4o system card, and AlpacaEval, while removing the CombLM, inference-time policy adapter, and Leonard nudging references. Positioning against proxy tuning, in-context alignment, and trained token-level collaboration remains substantially unchanged; consolidated duplicate references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The title changes, and substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, and experimental narrative are rewritten or streamlined. Discussion and conclusion become separate sections, limitations and ethical considerations are added, and the former Appendix A subsections are reorganized into Appendices A–F.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout and extensively restructures displays. Agreement and recall plots are redrawn, safety scores are incorporated into radar charts, model panels are removed, and new task-category and analytical tables appear. The original 37 appendix examples are retained as Tables 13–49 with revised formatting and pagination.

improvement.justification: The timing and discarded-token analyses better substantiate practical costs, while Llama-3 and constrained-instruction failures make applicability limits clearer. Correcting Algorithm 1 also improves reproducibility. These gains improve assessment of the retained method, but removing some control/threshold results and model panels reduces completeness, limiting the net improvement.
